raw.translational: Understanding the shared involvement of the coagulation cascade in both antithrombin deficiency and von Willebrand disease can inform therapeutic strategies. For instance, while anticoagulants are used for thrombosis in SERPINC1 deficiency, therapies aimed at restoring VWF function are used for bleeding in von Willebrand disease. Identifying the precise points of dysregulation within the common pathway could lead to novel, targeted treatments for specific hemostatic defects.

partners.diseaseBName: thrombophilia due to activated protein C resistance
partners.mechanism_chain: SERPINC1 (HGNC:10593) —DISRUPTS→ Antithrombin-thrombin inhibition (GO:0007596); Antithrombin-thrombin inhibition (GO:0007596) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal coagulation (HP:0011214); F5 (HGNC:3784) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal coagulation (HP:0011214); F5 R506Q (null) —DISRUPTS→ Activated Protein C pathway (GO:0007597); Activated Protein C pathway (GO:0007597) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombophilia (HP:0001939). Loss-of-function mutations in SERPINC1 impair antithrombin's ability to inhibit thrombin, leading to general coagulation abnormalities. Conversely, the F5 R506Q mutation (gain-of-function) impairs the ability of activated Protein C to cleave Factor Va, thereby reducing its inactivation and promoting a prothrombotic state. While both genes are involved in coagulation, the specific pathways and functional outcomes are distinct, leading to separate disease modules.

partners.mechanism_chain: SERPINC1 (HGNC:10620) —DECREASES→ Coagulation Cascade (REACT:R-HSA-8939318); Coagulation Cascade (REACT:R-HSA-8939318) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding (HP:00114055); F2 (HGNC:3759) —PRODUCES→ Thrombin (CHEBI:17650); Thrombin (CHEBI:17650) —DISRUPTS→ Coagulation Cascade (REACT:R-HSA-8939318); Thrombin (CHEBI:17650) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombophilia (HP:0001947).
